correctness.rationale: For every finite m>=3 and arbitrary simple H, all states in H have the same exit rate one to g and reset rate r to s, proving strong lumpability and full absorption-law invariance. Four explicit killed-chain backward equations yield the exact mean rational function. Its derivative numerator has a single positive root by Descartes sign rule (+,+,+,-,-), with negative value at zero, so the root is the unique global minimizer. Uniform polynomial scaling and simple-root expansion give the stated asymptotics. The standalone independent full-graph SymPy verifier passed 96 exact rational comparisons plus symbolic derivative/asymptotic checks; finite tests are corroboration, not exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is motivated by long excursions through an increasingly large trap coupled to a fixed-distance target. Every arbitrary internal-core rewiring leaves the full hitting law identical—a structural universality—not just one graph evaluation. A unique, finite optimal restart rate approaches sqrt(2), and the optimized mean is bounded at 4+2sqrt(2) despite the unrestarted mean 2m+3 diverging. Exact finite-size corrections and all-m uniqueness quantify a nontrivial design law not merely a normalizing identity. This is a natural complete family classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
